name: Wednesday
label: Dead Oceans
lede: A photography student in Asheville records a solo album under a British band's name, then builds a pedal-steel-and-feedback five-piece that ends up with the year's sixth-best album in Pitchfork's eyes.

eras.title: A solo project with a Bandcamp page
eras.text: Karly Hartzman starts Wednesday in Asheville as a one-person recording project, then gathers the town's musicians around it. The lineup she ends up with is why a band named after a British jangle-pop group sounds like Southern gothic with a pedal steel.

q: I learned how to play guitar watching Tiny Desk concerts.
years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: Karly Hartzman · NPR Tiny Desk: Wednesday · Stereogum: Band To Watch
years.h: [[Karly Hartzman|92ec14cd-1631-4724-98e8-b28da18360a8]] starts Wednesday as a solo project
years.p: She is a photography student at UNC Asheville who taught herself guitar by watching Tiny Desk concerts; the name comes from the British band [[The Sundays|9df32318-47d5-4df7-bc68-3ed9e15eb0f6]].
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Hartzman named the project after the Sundays and wanted to combine that band's vocals with the guitar noise of [[Swirlies|4ec4a033-ba44-41ca-8e09-3bf94fc08523]] and country writing. In a 2024 Tiny Desk introduction she credited the NPR series, and especially [[Mitski|fa58cf24-0e44-421d-8519-8bf461dcfaa5]]'s 2015 set, as her guitar school.

She grew up in Greensboro, North Carolina, and later told Stereogum she had picked up a ukulele in middle school.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: Karly Hartzman
years.h: [[MJ Lenderman|4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc]] sleeps over at Hartzman's family house
years.p: After a show, the guitarist crashes at her family's place; it is how the two Asheville songwriters meet, and the start of a six-year relationship.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Stereogum: Band To Watch
years.h: yep definitely: Hartzman and [[Daniel Gorham|e8f169df-d199-4262-b48a-cd42b9382423]] in a campus studio
years.p: The first Wednesday album is a duo record made with a college friend, and it goes up on Bandcamp before the band exists.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the release to January 31, 2018 and lists it as self-released. Paste and Stereogum both describe it as a solo debut recorded at a campus studio, blending dream-pop and indie rock.

years.src: Wikipedia: Karly Hartzman · Stereogum: Band To Watch
years.h: Hartzman sings in Diva Sweetly, a Pictures of Vernon spin-off
years.p: She joins the pop-punk band and plays on its 2019 album In The Living Room while Wednesday grows on the side.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: MJ Lenderman
years.h: How Do You Let Love Into the Heart That Isn't Split Wide Open
years.p: Wikipedia lists this December 2018 EP on Sub-Fi as the first Wednesday release with Lenderman on it.

eras.title: Five people, one lap steel
eras.text: Hartzman turns Wednesday into a real band around the Asheville scene: a drummer from the same shows, a pedal steel player from the same venue, a bassist, and the guitarist she is dating. The records get louder and stranger, and the label is a small Asheville imprint.

years.src: Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Mountain Xpress: Wednesday primes · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: Asheville does the hiring: [[Alan Miller|3dfb54e2-83c8-4e99-b44b-5fafb6dc0eae]] and [[Xandy Chelmis|cc52f05a-4006-44a8-8d0d-1ce50fe4942e]]
years.p: Paste says Hartzman met Miller at local shows and Chelmis while both worked at the Mothlight, the West Asheville venue that closed after nearly a decade.
years.xp:
Mountain Xpress reports she also interned at the Mothlight and got early opening slots there; opening for Speedy Ortiz in 2019 was, she said, a "we were losing our minds" night.

Wikipedia dates Miller from 2017 and Chelmis from 2020. Years in the sources differ, so the stints on this page follow Wikipedia.

years.src: Mountain Xpress: Wednesday primes · Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: I Was Trying to Describe You to Someone
years.p: The full-band debut arrives on Orindal Records, made in a bedroom studio; Gorham leaves for Prince Daddy & the Hyena around this time.
years.xp: Mountain Xpress calls the recording a bedroom-studio job; Paste says Gorham left after the record, while Wikipedia dates his stint to 2017–2019. Alan Miller told Paste that with Gorham the band had "very different styles at play".

years.src: Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Wikipedia: Twin Plagues
years.h: The lineup locks: Lenderman on lead guitar, [[Margo Schultz|66fd0ab1-1756-4dcf-9f39-5a0f626947f9]] on bass
years.p: Paste says Hartzman was a fan of his solo songs while working in food service before he became a full member around Twin Plagues.

years.src: Wikipedia: Twin Plagues · WUNC: The world according to Wednesday
years.h: Twin Plagues: the first Lenderman-era record
years.p: Recorded at Drop of Sun with Alex Farrar and Adam McDaniel, it earns Pitchfork's 7.4 and a No. 31 spot on Paste's 2021 list.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Kelly Liu described the sound as big and loud with an undercurrent of anxiety. Wikipedia credits Jake Lenderman as producer of "Ghost of a Dog", a cover of an Edie Brickell song.

The album also introduces Gary, a bar-fight character Hartzman brings back on Bleeds as "Gary's II".

years.src: WUNC: Why Asheville's Drop of Sun
years.h: Drop of Sun opens its Haywood Road studio
years.p: Founded by UNC Asheville grads Adam McDaniel and Alex Farrar in 2015, it becomes the room where Wednesday, Lenderman, Indigo De Souza and Angel Olsen record.

eras.title: Covers, a big scream, a big label
eras.text: A tribute record to the bands Wednesday learned from, then the song that changes the size of the room and a deal signed on the last day of tracking.

years.src: Stereogum: Hear Wednesday Cover
years.h: A covers album: Smashing Pumpkins to Gary Stewart
years.p: Wednesday plays songs by [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]], [[Medicine|0f24bcb0-8d37-409d-aed1-92bd4e5337ed]], [[Chris Bell|db6ac2f7-5bbb-4ed4-88f4-540d5b29542a]], [[Drive-By Truckers|8eae1e0a-1696-4532-9e3c-0a072217ef4c]], Roger Miller and others, recorded in Durham with Alli Rogers.
years.xp: Stereogum reports it was released on Orindal and includes three covers first recorded for Aquarium Drunkard in January 2022. Hartzman said the band wanted to repay in part the "huge debt" it owed those artists, and that the songs share sadness with humor.

years.cap: Karly Hartzman with the group Wednesday live in Grand Rapids, MI in 2023 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Bull Believer · Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Wikipedia: Rat Saw God
years.h: "Bull Believer" comes out, and Wednesday sign to Dead Oceans
years.p: The 8.5-minute single ends in Hartzman screaming; the band signed to Dead Oceans on the last day of tracking the album it leads.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the lyrics started from a George Jones episode of the podcast Cocaine & Rhinestones that included Spanish bullfighting history. Hartzman was self-conscious about screaming, so she recorded that section alone while the band played Tetris elsewhere in the studio; she said it was maybe the third time she had ever screamed.

Pitchfork later ranked it No. 92 of 2022's songs and Paste ranked it fifth.

eras.title: Year of the Rat
eras.text: The album that makes Wednesday a name outside the Southeast, and a year on the road that leaves the band a different shape.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rat Saw God · Nylon: Rock Band Wednesday · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: Rat Saw God: Pitchfork 8.8, No. 4 of the year
years.p: Recorded at Drop of Sun with Alex Farrar; Paste and Stereogum both put it first on their year-end lists.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Sam Sodomsky gave it 8.8; Metacritic assigned 89, per Wikipedia. Nylon reported that Pitchfork named it Best New Music. It is the last Wednesday album with Schultz, who also painted the six-foot oil painting used as the cover.

years.src: Nylon: Rock Band Wednesday · Mountain Xpress: Wednesday primes · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: [[Ethan Baechtold|6eaef41e-66a3-467c-a437-58b028b88058]] takes over bass from Margo Schultz
years.p: Baechtold is on the road for the spring 2023 U.S. and first European tours.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: Bull Believer
years.h: Primavera Sound: an anti-Amazon speech on Amazon's stage
years.p: Before "Bull Believer," Hartzman dedicated the song to warehouse workers who have ever been mistreated.
years.xp: Wikipedia and its Bull Believer article place the speech on the Amazon Music stage at Primavera Sound in Barcelona.

eras.title: Tiny Desk, and a breakup at the end of a tour
eras.text: The band is bigger than ever the year it changes shape. Hartzman and Lenderman separate on the road, and the group does not tell the public for a while.

years.src: NPR Tiny Desk: Wednesday
years.h: NPR Tiny Desk: the show that taught her guitar
years.p: Wednesday play "Chosen to Deserve", "Formula One" and "Bath County" with Chelmis on pedal steel, lap steel and banjo.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: MJ Lenderman · Paste: Wednesday Rejoice
years.h: Hartzman and Lenderman end six years together, in Tokyo
years.p: Wikipedia says they split while touring Japan and kept it from the rest of the band at first; most Bleeds songs were already written.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the breakup to March 2024 and says Lenderman revealed it in a July 2024 Guardian interview; Lenderman's page cites a February 2025 GQ interview. Hartzman told Paste that because they care about each other it was not hard to accept what he needed.

years.src: WUNC: Why Asheville's Drop of Sun
years.h: Hurricane Helene hits Asheville; the scene organizes
years.p: Drop of Sun cofounder Adam McDaniel's nonprofit Lamplight AVL raised $145,000 in artist grants, and a benefit compilation followed in March 2025.

eras.title: Bleeds
eras.text: The album Pitchfork puts sixth, made a month after the breakup by a band that keeps its guitarist in the studio and off the stage. Hartzman moves to Greensboro; the band lands on Colbert and, a year later, on a Weezer single.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · JamBase: Wednesday Toast
years.h: Lenderman stops touring with Wednesday, stays in the studio
years.p: He announces he will focus on his solo career; Hartzman calls him a non-negotiable part of the band's identity.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Lenderman said he would remain a full contributing member in the studio. Jake "Spyder" Pugh has since played lead guitar live.

years.src: Stereogum: Watch Wednesday Make · JamBase: Wednesday Toast
years.h: "Elderberry Wine" makes a Colbert TV debut
years.p: Lenderman joins the band on The Late Show, weeks after announcing he was leaving the road.
years.xp: Stereogum dates the performance to May 22 and JamBase to May 21; both note it was the band's first new music since Rat Saw God. Hartzman called the song about the potential of sweet things in life to become poison if not tended.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bleeds · BRICKS Magazine · Clash: The Way Love Goes · Album of the Year
years.h: Bleeds: Pitchfork 8.7, No. 6 of 2025
years.p: Recorded at Drop of Sun with Farrar a month after the breakup: Pitchfork gave it 8.7, then ranked it No. 6 of 2025.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Pitchfork 8.7, Metacritic 88, PopMatters 9 and Uncut 9; BRICKS quotes The Guardian calling it the year's best alt-rock album. Hartzman described it as the spiritual successor to Rat Saw God and the "quintessential Wednesday Creek Rock album".

Singles were "Elderberry Wine", "Wound Up Here (By Holdin On)", "Pick Up That Knife" and "Bitter Everyday". Hartzman said many songs were written while she and Lenderman were together and recorded a month after they split.

years.src: Paste: Wednesday Rejoice · WUNC: The world according to Wednesday
years.h: "Gary's II": a bar fight and a landlord remembered
years.p: The closer honors the late Gary King, Hartzman's Haw Creek landlord; she said she wanted to pass him on.

q: If Xandy was not in this band, Wednesday is over.
years.src: Paste: Wednesday Rejoice
years.h: The only member Hartzman says she can't lose
years.p: Chelmis, who met Hartzman working at the Mothlight, plays pedal steel, lap steel and banjo, and sings backing vocals.

years.src: Wikipedia: We Might as Well · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: Weezer's "We Might as Well Be Strangers" features Wednesday
years.p: Hartzman and Chelmis share the song from Weezer's twentieth album, the first Weezer collaboration since 2014.
